definition_quote.value: "Practice engineering" means to provide any service or creative work the performance of which requires education, training, and experience in the application of: (i) special knowledge of the mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences; and (ii) the principles and methods of engineering analysis and design.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice engineering" means to provide any service or creative work the performance of which requires education, training, and experience in the application of: (i) special knowledge of the mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences; and (ii) the principles and methods of engineering analysis and design.

value: inspection of construction to ensure compliance with specifications and drawings
methods_authorized.quote: "practice engineering" includes: (i) consultation; (ii) design; (iii) evaluation; (iv) inspection of construction to ensure compliance with specifications and drawings; (v) investigation; (vi) planning; and (vii) design coordination.

responsible_charge_defined.quote: "Responsible charge" means direct control and personal supervision of engineering that requires initiative, professional skill, and independent judgment.

firm_practice_allowed.quote: "Permit" means, unless the context requires otherwise, a permit issued by the Board to allow a corporation, partnership, or limited liability company to operate a business through which one or more professional engineers may practice engineering.

scope__exemptions_from_licensure.item: Federal government officers and employees practicing engineering in official capacity
Contractors executing work designed by a licensed engineer (construction execution only)
Building trades workers, craft workers, and construction superintendents/supervisors/inspectors performing customary duties
Employees or subordinates working under direct supervision of a licensed engineer
Engineers-in-training / engineer interns acting under supervision
Land surveyor interns
Teaching engineering, architectural, landscape architectural, or surveying courses at accredited institutions
Regulated transportation companies and public utilities (and their officers and employees) performing engineering for their own facilities
Engineering services incidental to the practice of architecture by licensed architects and their subordinates
Engineering services incidental to the practice of geology by licensed geologists and their subordinates
Practice of any other legally recognized profession or trade
Manufacturing, mining, public utility, research and development, or other industrial corporations performing engineering work incidental to their own products, systems, or services
Firms performing engineering services for themselves or their own subsidiaries/affiliates (in-house engineering)
Nonresident persons, firms, or corporations meeting specified out-of-state criteria
Real estate brokers or salespersons making appraisals and valuations of real estate
Alterations or repairs to buildings not affecting structural system or public health, safety, or welfare
Single-family and small residential dwellings of limited size
Agricultural work not required to be of public record
Revegetation, restoration, reclamation, rehabilitation, or erosion control for disturbed land not affecting public health, safety, or welfare
Maintenance or placement of plant material not affecting public health, safety, or welfare
Horticultural consultants and persons preparing planting plans for plant installations
Authorized designers of fire protection systems
Holders of temporary permits for engineering practice
Corporations, partnerships, LLCs, and LLPs offering professional engineering services through licensed principals (business entity exemption with certificate of authorization)
scope__exemptions_from_licensure.quote: "Permit" means, unless the context requires otherwise, a permit issued by the Board to allow a corporation, partnership, or limited liability company to operate a business through which one or more professional engineers may practice engineering.

scope__exemptions_from_licensure.item: Government employees inspecting residential structures as part of official duties
Persons performing home inspections solely for lender construction monitoring
Property managers inspecting their own managed residential structures without separate compensation
Small public works projects below a specified expenditure threshold
Licensed geologists practicing geology (not required to hold engineer license)
Persons with grandfathered or legacy licensure status in discontinued engineering branch titles
Boundary surveys on private land not intended as basis for engineering design
Professional engineers or engineer interns granted inactive status
Senior licensed professional engineers exempt from continuing education requirements
